chunk_findings.detail: The AST check iterates only `ast.parse(harness.read_text("utf-8")).body`, so it inspects only top-level import statements. If `ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py` has (or later gains) an `import urllib`, `import http`, or `import socket` nested inside a function, `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, `try:`, or other block, `roots` stays empty and the assertion passes. `importlinter` scans nested nodes, so `test_import_contracts` would still fail; this regression test therefore does not actually guard the contract against the drift it claims to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_harness.py:test_harness_imports_no_http_roots_and_holds_no_http_home_entry

chunk_findings.detail: The import scan only walks `ast.parse(...).body`, so it never sees imports nested in functions, classes, or `if` blocks. Given `harness.py` whose only network import is `def load(): import urllib.request` (or the same under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`), `roots` stays empty, the intersection assert passes, and the baseline assert also passes if no ignore line was added. That is the bug class this regression claims to lock: the module still imports `urllib`, while `test_harness_imports_no_http_roots_and_holds_no_http_home_entry` stays green.
